updates.title: Categories opens sorted by Name A to Z with an up arrow
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC26 alpha) exists, its name written in small letters.
Category {Category-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC26 Beta) exists, its name starting with a capital letter.
Category {Category-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC26 tier 9) exists.
Category {Category-D} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC26 Tier 10) exists.
Category {Category-E} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC26 TIER 100) exists.
No other category name starts with the same tag as these five (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC26).
The Default category {Default-category-A} (for example Uncategorized) shows the Default badge in the Categories list.
You are on a page other than Categories, so the test opens Categories afresh.
steps: Go to Settings and click Categories in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
Look at the Name column header.
Look at the first row of the list.
Scroll to {Category-A}, {Category-B}, {Category-C}, {Category-D} and {Category-E} and read their order from top to bottom.
results: Step 3: the Name column header shows an arrow pointing up (A to Z). No other header shows an arrow.
Step 4: the first row is {Default-category-A} with its Default badge, as it is today. It stays first whatever its name.

Step 5: the five rows read, top to bottom, {Category-A}, {Category-B}, {Category-C}, {Category-D}, {Category-E} (with the examples: alpha, Beta, tier 9, Tier 10, TIER 100). Capital letters make no difference (alpha comes before Beta) and numbers are in counting order (9, then 10, then 100).
Step 5: the order is not character by character. That would read Beta, TIER 100, Tier 10, alpha, tier 9, and is a failure.

quotes: The Name column header is sortable.
When the page first opens, the list is sorted by name in ascending order, A to Z.
The name sort ignores whether letters are upper case or lower case, and compares numbers inside a name as numbers, so `Tier 9` comes before `Tier 10`.
When the page first opens, the Name column header shows an ascending arrow.

The Default category is always the first row in the list. It holds that position under the Name sort and under the QuickBooks Products and Services sort, in ascending and in descending order alike, and it holds it after a reload in place. When a search term is typed it is first whenever it is among the matching rows; a term that does not match its name leaves it out of the results, as today, and it is never forced into them. This is the behavior the Categories list has in production today and it does not change.
Given categories named "Zinc" and "alternator", when sorted ascending by name, then "alternator" comes before "Zinc".
Default category - the category row named "Uncategorized", which carries the "Default" badge and cannot be edited.
